title.content: The Art of Destruction: Burning Down a City

text.content:
We're Gold! Those are the best two words you can hear while working on a game aside from the office stampede inducing "foods here"...but getting to that point took a tremendous amount of time and effort from the team, especially in these last couple of months. Now that I have some free time I can share with you a little bit of what went on in the last months of making Infamous, at least from my point of view...
My role at Sucker Punch, is to make the texture artists' jobs more difficult. This mostly entails modeling object, creating new areas for the game, and most importantly making them as insanely detailed as possible. In short, I'm what the raccon overlords at Sucker Punch call an Environment Modeler.

title.content: A Brief Pictorial History of Empire City, Vol. 1 A.K.A. Designing a New IP Always Makes a Mess of the Cutting Room Floor

text.content:
Matt Longest (Mostly Gameplay) Programmer Sucker Punch Productions
Hello, and welcome to Empire City! My name is Matt, and I will be your tour guide. We are going to take a trip back to 2006, when Sucker Punch was in pre-production for a little project known as "True Hero".
(Screen 1)
Before we had our PS3 Engine, we were doing prototypes on the PS2 with our Sly Engine. Here we see Sly making a daring leap off of a rooftop. Prototypes like this allowed us to identify that cross-town navigation was going to be an interesting challenge for out hero. This eventually (over a few years) led to riding on the elevated train cars and electrical wires.
(Screen 2)

(Screen 1)
If your answer is "yes", then keep on reading! In this blog entry I'm going to talk a little about the Megawatt Hammer, one of Cole McGrath's many electric powers in inFAMOUS.
To start with, my name is Darren Bridges, and I'm a game designer at Sucker Punch. I worked on several of Cole's powers, and the Megawatt Hammer is one of my favorites. From the beginning, we'd planned for it to be a "rocket launcher"-style power that players would unlock midway through the game. There were two main issues I still needed to resolve: how would it be cooler than a standard rocket weapon, and how would it evolve along the good and evil upgrade paths?
Our general guideline for power growth in inFAMOUS is that good powers should become more precise and controlled, and evil powers should become more chaotic and destructive. Let's talk about the evil upgrade path first, since I started this whole thing by tempting you with explosions.

title.content: The Interactive World of InFAMOUS... Sounds of Destruction

text.content:
For a Sound Designer, working on a game like inFAMOUS is a creative dream come true. You get to design sounds for horribly mutated creatures, create an apocalyptic ambient soundscape, and of course, you get to make sounds for an awesome set of super powers. As Sucker Punch's Junior Sound designer, however, my tasks usually included working on the more easily overlooked sounds (and even some that are impossible to miss!). As I soon found out though, in a game as immensely detailed as inFAMOUS, there's room for creativity everywhere.
Empire City is full of interactivity. If you see something that you think you want to break, more likely than not you can. You can smash boxes, dismember mannequins, blow up fire extinguishers, and destroy benches, and that's just getting started. As a class of objects that needed sound, we collectively called these things breakables, and I was responsible for designing the sound effects. for all of them.
One of my early tasks after joining the inFAMOUS team was to design sound for the refrigerator on Zeke's roof. Although more of an interactive object than something to destroy, it still fell under my purview, and is a great example of the detail put into bringing seemingly simple objects to life. When Cole punches or zaps the refrigerator, it bounces around a little and the door simply opens
